title: Hairline diagonal cracking above a door — cause uncertain, no hypothesis
why: Hairline diagonal cracking from a door head is consistent with shrinkage/thermal movement, with lintel deflection, or with structural movement. Nothing distinguishes them here. The finding must not call it structural, must not propose Hazard 29, and must not price a make-good as if the cause were settled.

room.name: Hallway
room.note: Hairline diagonal crack from the top corner of the living room door frame up towards the ceiling, maybe 600mm long. Not stepped, no displacement, decoration intact either side. No other cracking seen in the house.

transcripts: Hall, hairline crack coming off the top corner of the door into the living room, runs diagonally up maybe six hundred. Not stepped, no displacement, can't get a coin in it. Nothing else like it anywhere in the property that I saw.

must_not_happen.label: no structural diagnosis from a hairline crack
no structural-collapse hazard from a hairline crack
no whole-ceiling make-good for a 600 mm wall crack

allowed_uncertainty: Shrinkage/thermal movement as preferred at low/medium with lintel deflection and structural movement open; or no preferred cause.
reviewer_notes: 600 mm is a stated figure and may appear in the prose; any other dimension would be invented.
